title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Overview (total net revenue +44%)
key_points: FY2022 net revenue was $23.6 billion, an increase of 44% compared to FY2021 net revenue of $16.4 billion.

The increase was driven by a 64% increase in Data Center segment revenue (higher EPYC server processor sales), a 21% increase in Gaming segment revenue (higher semi-custom product sales), and a significant increase in Embedded segment revenue from inclusion of Xilinx embedded product sales.

Growth was partially offset by a 10% decrease in Client segment revenue due to lower processor shipments driven by a weak PC market and significant inventory correction actions across the PC supply chain.
Gross margin as a percentage of net revenue was 45% in 2022 versus 48% in 2021, primarily due to amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition.
Operating income was $1.3 billion in 2022 versus $3.6 billion in 2021; net income was $1.3 billion versus $3.2 billion.
In February 2022 AMD completed the strategic acquisition of Xilinx; in May 2022 it acquired Pensando Systems.

This growth was partially offset by a 10% decrease in Client segment revenue primarily due to lower processor shipments driven by a weak PC market and significant inventory correction actions across the PC supply chain.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Results of Operations: segment reporting change and Data Center / Client commentary
key_points: During Q2 of fiscal 2022 AMD changed its reporting segments; it now reports four reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded.
Data Center net revenue of $6 billion in 2022 increased by 64% versus $3.7 billion in 2021, primarily driven by higher sales of EPYC server processors.
Data Center operating income was $1.8 billion in 2022 versus $991 million in 2021, driven by higher revenue partially offset by higher operating expenses.
Client net revenue of $6.2 billion in 2022 decreased by 10% versus $6.9 billion in 2021, driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipments, partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price.

The Client unit shipment decrease was due to challenging PC market conditions and significant inventory correction across the PC supply chain in the second half of 2022; the ASP increase was driven by a richer mix of Ryzen mobile processor sales.
Client operating income was $1.2 billion in 2022 versus $2.1 billion in 2021, driven by lower revenue and higher operating expenses.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Note 5: unaudited pro forma information basis of presentation (Xilinx and Pensando)
key_points: The 10-K presents unaudited pro forma information combining AMD with the historical results of Xilinx and Pensando.
The pro forma information is presented on the basis of AMD's fiscal year: Xilinx's fiscal year ended on the Saturday nearest March 31, and Pensando's fiscal year ended on January 31.

The twelve months ended December 31, 2022 includes Xilinx results for the twelve-month period beginning January 2, 2022 through December 31, 2022 and Pensando results for January 1, 2022 through December 31, 2022.
The twelve months ended December 25, 2021 includes Xilinx results for the twelve months ended January 1, 2022 and Pensando results for the twelve months ended December 31, 2021.

The unaudited pro forma information is for informational purposes only and is not necessarily indicative of results that would have been achieved if the acquisitions were completed at the beginning of fiscal year 2021.
Pro forma adjustment: amortization expense of acquired Xilinx inventory fair value step-up of $184 million in fiscal year 2021 and no Xilinx inventory fair value step-up expense in fiscal year 2022.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Client segment: unit shipment vs average selling price decomposition
key_points: Client net revenue of $6.2 billion in FY2022 decreased 10% vs $6.9 billion in FY2021.
The decrease was primarily driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipments, partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price.
The unit shipment decrease was due to challenging PC market conditions and significant inventory correction across the PC supply chain experienced during the second half of 2022.
The increase in average selling price was primarily driven by a richer mix of Ryzen mobile processor sales.
Client operating income was $1.2 billion vs $2.1 billion in FY2021, driven by lower revenue and higher operating expenses.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Gaming and Embedded segment drivers; All Other composition
key_points: Gaming net revenue of $6.8 billion in FY2022 increased 21% vs $5.6 billion in FY2021, driven by higher semi-custom product sales due to higher demand for gaming console SoCs.

Gaming growth was partially offset by lower gaming graphics sales due to a decrease in unit shipments driven by soft consumer demand given weakened macroeconomic conditions in the second half of 2022.

Embedded net revenue of $4.6 billion in FY2022 increased significantly vs $246 million in FY2021, primarily driven by the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product revenue following the February 2022 Xilinx acquisition.
Embedded operating income was $2.3 billion vs $44 million in FY2021, primarily driven by the inclusion of Xilinx embedded product revenue.

All Other operating loss of $5.0 billion in FY2022 primarily consisted of $3.5 billion of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, $1.1 billion of stock-based expense and $42 million of acquisition-related costs.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Inventory valuation policy and net inventory balance (Critical Accounting Estimates / CAM)
key_points: AMD values inventory at standard cost adjusted to approximate the lower of actual cost or estimated net realizable value, using assumptions about future demand and market conditions.

The 10-K notes that if inventory is written down in a period and demand rises, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales, resulting in a net benefit to gross margin in that period.
Net inventory balance at December 31, 2022 was $3,771 million.
The 10-K does not disclose a specific FY2022 or Q4 2022 inventory write-down dollar amount.

title: AMD FY2022 Form 10-K — Risk factors: Client revenue decline from PC weakness and inventory correction
key_points: AMD states it experienced a decline in Client segment revenue as a result of weak PC market macroeconomic conditions and inventory correction actions across the PC supply chain in the second half of 2022.
AMD notes uncertainty in the worldwide economic environment (inflation, interest rates, recession) may negatively impact consumer confidence and spending, causing customers to postpone purchases.
raw_excerpt: We experienced a decline in our Client segment revenue as a result of weak PC market macroeconomic conditions and inventory correction actions across the PC supply chain in the second half of 2022.
